name: Free fall in uniform gravity (no air resistance)

formula.relation: net force on the body, m dv/dt = -m g. NOT a transcription of formulaTeX above, which states the integrated position form y(t); the two describe the same physics at different levels of integration and must not be compared as if they were the same expression

conventions: y positive upward, measured from chosen origin
v_0 positive when initial velocity points upward
expectedLimits: landing (y = 0, y_0 > 0): t_land = (v_0 + sqrt(v_0^2 + 2 g y_0))/g
energy conservation: (1/2) v^2 + g y = const along trajectory

machine formula: `formula.expr` gives the net force -m g (the equation of motion m dv/dt = -m g), which is the form a drag-corrected hypothesis reduces to as its drag coefficient vanishes. formulaTeX above states the integrated position form; the two describe the same physics at different levels of integration, and only the force form is what a limit claim compares against
references: Halliday, Resnick & Walker — Fundamentals of Physics, ch.2
